name: NGC 1365 Cepheid 97780
description: A Cepheid in the galaxy NGC 1365 that pulsates every 20.7 days, found by the Hubble Space Telescope.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 20.708 d in Hoffmann et al. (2016), ApJ 830, 10, table 5; not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 20.708 d in Hoffmann et al. (2016), ApJ 830, 10, table 5; not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own temperatures of its Cepheids

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of NGC 1365, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2022ApJS..261....2K; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Riess et al. (2016), ApJ 826, 56, table 5: NGC 1365's Cepheid distance modulus 31.307 +/- 0.057 mag, 10^(mu/5 + 1) pc

text.card: A Cepheid in the galaxy NGC 1365, 18 million parsecs away, that swells and shrinks every 20.7 days.
text.introduction: The Hubble Space Telescope found it and timed its pulsation at 20.7 days. Its galaxy's distance, 18.3 million parsecs, was measured from Cepheids like it.
text.locator: table 5, Gal N1365, ID 97780: Per; Riess et al. (2016), ApJ 826, 56, table 5, N1365: mu_Ceph

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius
Its radius and temperature are what Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33's relations for Galactic Cepheids give at its period; no measurement of this star's size or temperature exists
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within NGC 1365 is not measured
